questions.text:
Consider the Deterministic Finite-state Automaton (DFA) [latex]A[/latex] shown below. The DFA runs on the alphabet {0, 1}, and has the set of states {s, p, q, r}, with s being the start state and p being the only final state.

Which one of the following regular expressions correctly describes the language accepted by [latex]A[/latex]?
questions.solution:
From s: 0 goes to dead state r, so a string must start with 1 (reaching final state p).
At p: 0 loops on p; 1 goes to q, and from q only another 1 returns to p (0 goes to r).

So after the first 1, we repeat "0" or "11": [latex]1(0+11)^*[/latex].

Answer: [latex]1(0+11)^*[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]1(0^*11)^*[/latex]
[latex]0(0 + 1)^*[/latex]
[latex]1(0 + 11)^*[/latex]
[latex]1(110^*)^*[/latex]

questions.solution:
Look at each language closely:
- [latex]L_1[/latex]: n can be 0, so taking n = 0, [latex]L_1=\{w\}=(a+b)^*[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] regular.
- [latex]L_2[/latex]: [latex]|w|\ge1[/latex] and x can be anything, so it is enough that the string starts and ends with the same symbol with something in between: [latex]a(a+b)^+a+b(a+b)^+b[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] regular.

Both are regular, hence also context-free. So options 1, 2 and 3 are true; "context-free but not regular" is false.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3

questions.text: Which of the following is/are undecidable?
questions.solution:
Options 1-3 ask about a non-trivial property of the language of a TM (equality, regularity, accepting everything). By Rice's theorem they are undecidable.

Option 4 is decidable: in 1073 steps a TM can read at most the first 1073 input symbols, so it is enough to simulate M for 1073 steps on the finitely many strings of length up to 1073.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Given two Turing machines M1 and M2 , decide if L(M1 ) = L(M2 ).
Given a Turing machine M , decide if L(M ) is regular.
Given a Turing machine M , decide if M accepts all strings.
Given a Turing machine M , decide if M takes more than 1073 steps on every string.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- A subset of an RE language need not be recursive (e.g. the halting language is a subset of [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex]) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- If [latex]L[/latex] and [latex]\bar L[/latex] are both RE, run both recognizers in parallel; one must accept, so [latex]L[/latex] is recursive [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Every CFL is recursive and recursive languages are closed under complement [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- [latex]L_1\cap L_2[/latex] is regular, and every regular language is deterministic context-free [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Every subset of a recursively enumerable language is recursive.
If a language [latex]L[/latex] and its complement [latex]\bar{L}[/latex] are both recursively enumerable, then [latex]L[/latex] must be recursive.
Complement of a context-free language must be recursive.
If [latex]L_1[/latex] and [latex]L_2[/latex] are regular, then [latex]L_1 \cap L_2 [/latex]must be deterministic context-free.
